newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds rise with Europe, seen holding level.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds rise with Europe, seen holding level.

text.p: Danish bond prices crept up on Wednesday, following other European markets, with the mood positive and prices set to keep their levels up to the close.

"The market undertone is palpably better than it was yesterday. I think we are going to see the current price levels hold until the end of the day, the only uncertain factor is the afternoon's U.S. third quarter GDP data," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.08 point from Tuesday's close at 107.78, yielding 6.83 percent in turnover of 1.1 billion crowns while its December future rose 0.20 point to 107.34 with 96 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.42 point to 84.95.
The crown traded at 3.8435 per mark at 1105 gmt, unchanged from the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 87 during the course of the morning.
